title: Adaptive Flow Control and Attention Alignment for Continuous Batching
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Reduce 99th percentile tail latency for mixed-workload continuous batching by introducing an adaptive admission flow controller that uses model/kernel latency signatures and attention alignment heuristics to shape prefill and decode scheduling.
goals: Bring 99th percentile end-to-end latency down by >=35% for mixed short+long sequence workloads under 2x baseline load
Preserve or improve aggregate throughput (tokens/sec) within 5% of current baseline
Avoid increased variance for high-priority (SLA) tenants; ensure fairness across priority classes
success_metrics: p99 inference latency (end-to-end) reduced by >=35% on benchmark suite A
no more than 3% regression in total tokens/sec on standard clusters
SLA tenant tail-latency unaffected (p99 within existing SLAs) across 95% of runs
design_notes: Observations: kernel selection currently uses static affinity per model variant which fails to capture transient queueing effects; attention KV cache layout and kernel warmup cause small prefill bursts to pay high overheads

Approach overview: decouple admission control from decode scheduling. Admission controller will consult lightweight per-model kernel latency distributions and current kernel warmup state to decide immediate admission vs micro-window deferral. A compact attention-alignment heuristic will co-locate similar attention patterns into the same batch to reduce KV cache pressure and vector kernel misses.

Kernel hints: add 'latency_quartiles' in model profile and expose 'warmup_score' from kernel manager. Use these hints in a scoring function: admission_score = alpha * (normalized_expected_latency) + beta * (warmup_penalty) + gamma * (tenant_priority_factor).

Trade-offs: deferring small prefill requests (<= 16 tokens) reduces tail but adds small added latency for those requests; to avoid unfair delays we apply tenant-aware bucketing and a max-deferral window of 20ms for P2/P3 tenants and 5ms for P0/P1 tenants.

Attention alignment: compute a lightweight fingerprint of attention head shapes (sparse/dense hint), sequence length buckets, and token-type (chat/system) to prefer batching inputs with compatible KV layouts. This is a heuristic (fast, constant-time) to avoid costly per-request kernel probing.

Kernel selection: introduce transient kernel binding that allows the runtime to change kernel variant between prefill and decode if runtime profiling indicates a different kernel will be more efficient at decode lengths. Must be guarded by consistency checks for KV cache formats.
Compatibility: fall back to existing admission path when profile data is missing or when 'safe-mode' environment variable is set for customer Private deployments.
implementation_plan: Spike: 1 week - implement admission_score prototype and local simulator to reproduce tail behavior (benchmark on perf lab)
Phase 1: 2 weeks - runtime admission controller that consults kernel latency histograms and enforces deferral windows; metric emission added (per-tenant admission decisions)
Phase 2: 3 weeks - attention alignment fingerprinting and batcher coupling; integrate with continuous batcher to prefer aligned groups
Phase 3: 2 weeks - transient kernel binding for prefill->decode path with KV format checks and canary rollout on dev cluster
Phase 4: 1 week - run long-duration soak tests, collect regressions, tune alpha/beta/gamma weights, and prepare rollout plan
Rollout: staged canary: dev -> staging -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on metric regression
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller deployed to staging and passes soak tests (48h) without regressions
Benchmarks show p99 improvement >= target on mixed-short-long suite vs baseline commit (link to benchmark run in related_links)
No more than 2% regression in total throughput across standard hardware profiles
All telemetry exposed: admission decisions, deferral counts, alignment-hit-rate, kernel-switch events
Automated feature flag present for emergency kill-switch and per-customer opt-out
dependencies: ENG-70158 (KV format stability checks and compatibility matrix)
risks: Mis-tuned deferral weights could increase median latency for latency-sensitive tenants; mitigation: conservative defaults and per-tenant caps
Attention fingerprint collisions could batch incompatible inputs leading to decode slowdowns; mitigation: fallback to size-only batching after threshold
Transient kernel binding complexity could cause KV cache incompatibilities; mitigation: strict format/version checks and logging with auto-revert
Observable metrics volume increase; mitigation: selective sampling and aggregation at the admission controller
